skills.title: Templates — state the shape, don't assemble it
skills.trigger: Writing a multi-line string a program emits — generated code, a config block, a report, a message. Read this the moment you find yourself building one line at a time and joining, so the OUTPUT stays readable in the source that produces it.
skills.intro:
A template is a picture of its output. Write it as one — a heredoc, at its real
indentation — and a reader sees what the program will emit. Assemble it from a list of line
fragments and they have to run it in their head.
skills.summary: a multi-line string is a heredoc that SHOWS its output, never a list of line fragments joined.
skills.principle:
The test is simple: **can you see the output by reading the source?**

A heredoc can be read as the thing it produces. Its indentation is real whitespace, its blank lines
are blank lines, and the parts that vary are interpolations sitting exactly where they will land. The
source and the output have the same shape, so a reader checks them against each other at a glance.

An array of line fragments joined with a newline has neither property:

- The **delimiters come apart.** `'/**'` and `' */'` are separate elements with the body between
  them, so a docblock is not visibly a docblock — it is three unrelated strings that happen to be
  adjacent.
- The **indentation is spelled**, not laid out. `'    $config->disable('` asks the reader to count
  characters inside a quote instead of seeing alignment.
- The **escapes fight the interpolation.** `"\${$var} = function (Config \$config): void {"` has to
  be decoded before you know what it emits.
- The **join is somewhere else.** `implode("\n", $lines)` can be ten lines away, so nothing at the
  array itself says these are LINES at all. Change the separator and every element silently means
  something different.

### The fix

State it once, as a heredoc, and interpolate what varies:

```php
$body = implode("\n", $entries);   // the part that is genuinely computed

return <<<PHP
    /**
     * {$purpose}
     */
    \${$var} = function (Config \$config): void {
        \$config->disable(
    {$body}
        );
    };
    PHP;
```

The fixed shape is now visible and the computed part is one hole in it.

### What is NOT this sin

- **Joining values the program computed.** `implode("\n", array_map(fn ($f) => $f->label, $findings))`
  is a list being presented, not a template — there is no fixed shape for a heredoc to state.
- **Joining into ONE line.** `implode(', ', $columns)` builds a value, not a layout.
- **A pair.** Two lines is not a template; its shape is already visible.
- **A genuinely dynamic set of lines**, where which lines appear is the whole point. Reach for a
  heredoc per line-kind if the lines themselves have shape; otherwise leave it.

### `sprintf` is the small sibling

For a ONE-line string with holes, `sprintf('%s (%d)', $name, $count)` states the shape the same way
concatenation does not. The principle is identical: put the literal in one piece and let the values
sit in it.

related.reason: the same instinct one scale down: say a thing once, in the form a reader can check.
a shape worth stating repeatedly is usually a type, not a string.

skills.title: Type honesty — the type must not lie
skills.trigger: A type must tell the truth about the value. Don't fake optionality — a `?T` / nullable that the design always has set, which the code then immediately defends against (`?->`, `?? <fake>`, null-checks) or stashes as mutable scratch state and restores. The defence is the tell that the type is lying. Make the type carry the certainty: pass the value as a parameter, hold it non-nullable, or wrap per-call context in a value object. Read this BEFORE you add a nullable field set later in a method, or reach for `$this->scratch?->… ?? false`.
skills.intro:
A `?T` that is never actually null is a lie the whole codebase pays for. Every reader has to re-prove the
value is there — `?->`, `?? <default>`, an `if ($x === null)` — and one of those defaults silently answers
a question for a state that can't happen. Make the type say what the design guarantees.
skills.summary: a type must not lie: don't fake optionality — a `?T` the design always has set, then defended with `?->`/`?? <fake>` or stashed as save/restore scratch state. Make the type certain (pass it, hold it non-nullable, a per-call value object). The complement of `absence`.
skills.principle:
When a value is **always present where it's used**, the type should say so: a non-nullable field, a
constructor parameter, a method parameter, a value object. Hedging it as a **nullable that's set later** —
or a **mutable field used as per-call scratch** — pushes the certainty back onto every caller, who re-
establishes it with defensive code. The defensive code is the smell; the cure is upstream, in the type.

This is the complement of [`absence`](../absence/SKILL.md): *absence* says model genuine missingness
honestly (Option / empty / throw); *type-honesty* says don't manufacture missingness the design doesn't
have. A value that's truly optional belongs in `absence`. A value that's always there but typed `?T` for
convenience belongs here.

### What is NOT this sin

- **A genuinely optional, constructor-injected collaborator** read with `?->… ?? …`. If `$this->logger` is
  injected once and may legitimately be absent, defaulting it is a Null-Object choice, not a masked
  invariant — that's `absence` territory, not a type lie.
- **Modelling real missingness** — a finder that may find nothing, a config that may be unset. Use
  `absence`: `Option`, an empty default, or a throw. The lie is only when the value is *certain* and typed
  as if it weren't.

### The tell

You're re-proving, on every read, something the design already guarantees: `?->` on your own field, a
`?? <literal>` whose branch can't be reached, a `$prev = $this->x; … $this->x = $prev`. Ask: *is this value
ever actually absent here?* If no, the type is lying — move the value into the signature, a non-nullable
field, or a value object, and delete the defence.

related.reason: the complement: absence models a genuine maybe-missing; this kills a FAKE one.
make the type certain where the value is born, not defended at every read.

skills.title: Value objects — give related data a type
skills.trigger: WHEN to give data a type instead of passing it loose — an `array<string,mixed>` bag, 3+ values that always travel together (a data clump), a string-indexed structured array, primitive obsession, or a too-long parameter list all want a typed object. Read this BEFORE you pass or return an untyped array, add another parameter to a crowded signature, or write `$arr['key']` on a structured array. (How to WRITE the class is `spatie-data`; this is when to make one.)
skills.intro:
Data that travels together is a **thing**, not a loose pile of arrays and primitives. The moment a
cluster of values is passed around, returned, or reached into by string keys, it wants a name and a type.
skills.summary: give related data a type: no loose `array<string,mixed>` bags, no data clumps, no primitive obsession. (Decide the type; then `spatie-data` is how to write it.)
skills.principle:
Data that travels together is a **thing**, not a loose pile of arrays and primitives. The moment a cluster
of values is passed around, returned, or reached into by string keys, it wants a name and a type — the type
IS the documentation, the validation, and the contract, all enforced by the compiler instead of by every
reader's memory.

Reach for a type when you: pass or return an `array<string, mixed>` bag whose keys are an undocumented
contract; pass three or more values that always travel together (a data clump); reach into a structured array
by string key (`$entry['title']`) instead of a typed object; keep adding parameters to an already-crowded
signature instead of grouping them; or pass a bare primitive that is really a concept — a `string $email`, a
`string $currency` + `int $amount`, a `string $key` with format rules — that wants a value object owning its
own validation.

Introduce the type at the boundary that first receives the data, or the method that first assembles it — not
several steps later, after it has been passed around as a loose array. A value object
introduced late just relabels data everyone already mishandled. This is fix-at-the-source applied to shape.

related.reason: introduce the type where the data is born, not downstream.
once you've decided it's a DTO, that skill is *how* to write it (and its honest-field-types rule keeps the new type from being a fresh all-nullable bag).
the new type's fields still answer "can this be missing?" honestly.

sins.name: archaeology-comment
sins.description: History/archaeology comments ("formerly / used to be / refactored / no longer an X / was extracted")
sins.rule: Comment what the code IS now, never its history — no "formerly/used to be/refactored/no longer an X" archaeology; git holds the past.

sins.name: array-bag
sins.description: String-indexing (`$arr['key']`) a structured array param instead of giving it a name — the type was never defined.
sins.rule: Give a structured array a typed value object — never read a named field by string key off an `array` param.
sins.suggestion: A Spatie `Data` object built via `::from($array)`.

sins.name: array-return-bag
sins.description: Returning a multi-field string-keyed array literal (a bag that should be a value object)
sins.rule: Return a typed value object, not a multi-field string-keyed array literal.
sins.suggestion: Return a Spatie `Data` object via `::from(...)`.

sins.name: assembled-template
sins.description: A multi-line template assembled as an array of line fragments and joined with a newline — the output is unreadable in the source that emits it
sins.rule: State a fixed multi-line string as a heredoc, at its real indentation, and interpolate what varies — never as a list of line fragments joined by a newline.
sins.suggestion: A heredoc (`<<<PHP` / `<<<'PHP'`), with the computed part as one interpolation.

sins.name: bare-state-predicate
sins.description: A `bool` about the object's own state named as a bare verb — `binds()`, `spins()` — where a question belongs
sins.rule: A `bool` answering about the object itself wears a question: `isBound()`, `isSpinning()`, `hasParent()`, `awaitsAnswer()`. (A predicate that takes what it compares against — `contains(\$item)`, `matches(\$name)` — is already a sentence and stays as it is.)
sins.suggestion: make it a question: `is…`, `has…`, `can…`, `awaits…`

sins.name: blank-string-default
sins.description: `string $x = ''` standing in for absence — then asked `$x === ''`
sins.rule: Model a value that may not be there in the type; never default a total `string` to `''` and read that blank back as "missing".
sins.suggestion: Say it in the type — `?string $x = null`, or an `Option<string>` — so the blank is not a value the reader has to decode.

sins.name: blank-string-on-the-wire
sins.description: A `string` field sent over the wire whose TypeScript reader has to check `=== ''` to mean "missing" — only that reader knows the blank stands for absence.
sins.rule: A field that crosses the wire says absence in its TYPE; never ship a blank for the far side to decode as missing.
sins.suggestion: `?string $x = null` on the shape, and the reader asks `x == null` — one spelling of absence, agreed by both sides.

sins.name: bloated-docblock
sins.description: Multi-paragraph class docblock (class too big)
sins.rule: Keep a class docblock to one tight paragraph — a multi-paragraph essay means the class does too much.

sins.name: cancelled-coalesce
sins.description: `??` cancelled by the comparison it sits in — `($x ?? '') !== ''`
sins.rule: Ask about absence directly (`$x !== null`); never coalesce to a value only to compare against that same value.
sins.suggestion: Say both halves out loud — `$x !== null && $x !== ''` — or make the value non-nullable at its source so only one question is left.

sins.name: ceremony-docblock
sins.description: Docblock that only restates the typed signature (`@param Type $x`, no description)
sins.rule: A docblock must add meaning beyond the signature — drop `@param Type $x` lines that only restate an already-typed parameter.

sins.name: coalesced-loop-subject
sins.description: `foreach ($x[$k] ?? [] as …)` — the absence check buried in the loop header instead of stated as a guard
sins.rule: State an absent collection at the top as a guard (early return); don't bury `?? []` in a `foreach` header.
sins.suggestion: An early `return` when the collection is absent, so the loop iterates something that is THERE.

sins.name: computed-boolean-argument
sins.description: A parameter that's just true/false, computed by every caller from the same object it could be given instead.
sins.rule: Take the SUBJECT and ask it — never a bool every caller derives from that same object.
sins.suggestion: swap the flags for the object the callers already hold: `CornerInset::for($editor)`

sins.name: concurrent-subclass
sins.description: Class `extends Concurrent` instead of composing `Concurrent<self>`
sins.rule: Compose `Concurrent<self>` via a `::for()` factory; never `extends Concurrent`.
sins.suggestion: Compose `Concurrent<self>` behind a `::for($id)` factory.

sins.name: conditional-array-spread
sins.description: An array built by spreading a conditional element — `...($x ? ['k' => $x] : [])` or `array_merge($base, $cond ? [...] : [])` — a ternary-and-empty-array trick that really just means "include this when the value is present."
sins.rule: Don't spread a `cond ? [...] : []` to conditionally include a key. Give the target a null-dropping variadic factory (`::of(mixed ...$values)` that filters out nulls) and pass the value as a named arg — an absent one vanishes with no ternary.
sins.suggestion: Replace `[...$base, ...($x !== null ? ['k' => $x] : [])]` with a `::of(k: $x, …)` factory that drops null-valued arguments.

sins.name: const-class-enum
sins.description: A class of 2+ scalar `const`s and nothing else — a closed set hand-rolled as constants instead of a native enum
sins.rule: Seal a closed set of values as a native backed enum, not a class of scalar `const`s or loose strings.
sins.suggestion: A native `enum X: string` with the values as cases.

sins.name: constructor-side-effect
sins.description: A constructor that performs a side effect on a collaborator and throws away the result, so simply creating the object changes something outside it.
sins.rule: Let a constructor establish what the object IS; never let building one change anything outside it.
sins.suggestion: Keep the collaborator as a field and act on it from the method that someone actually calls.

sins.name: converted-argument
sins.description: A parameter typed as the already-converted form instead of the raw value, so every call site repeats the same conversion before calling it (e.g. `Raises::of(ClassAlias::of($interaction), …)`).
sins.rule: Declare the parameter in the form callers already have, and do the conversion inside the callee — so the conversion rule lives in one place.
sins.suggestion: Move the wrapper into the callee and widen the parameter to the type being wrapped; every call site then passes the value it means, and a site that forgets the conversion stops compiling.

sins.name: coupled-fields
sins.description: A class's own fields always change and get checked together — one concept split across several fields — and should be folded into a single value object.
sins.rule: Fields that always change together are really one type — extract them into a value object and use it directly; don't keep a field that just duplicates a nested object's property.
sins.suggestion: Fold the co-moving fields into one value object (name the existing type when the clump already is one); drop a field that duplicates a nested object's property.

sins.name: dangling-doc-reference
sins.description: A docblock `{@see}`/`{@link}` cross-references a FIRST-PARTY class that does not exist in the codebase — documentation pointing at a name that was renamed or removed, never at what the code actually is
sins.rule: A `{@see}`/`{@link}` must resolve to a real class. A cross-reference to a first-party class the codebase no longer declares is stale documentation — repoint it at the current class or delete it. (References into another vendor namespace are left alone; they can't be verified here.)

sins.name: data-clump
sins.description: The same 3+ scalar params threaded through 2+ classes (a recurring data clump → one object)
sins.rule: Bundle values that always travel together into one object; don't thread 3+ of them as separate params.
sins.suggestion: A value object the params fold into (`Money::of()`, `NodePosition`).

sins.name: de-nulled-finder
sins.description: A finder that returns `null` for both "missing" and "broken" instead of throwing — the kind of `?T` finder whose callers all end up de-nulling it.
sins.rule: Decide absence where the value is found — if every caller ends up de-nulling a `?T` finder, make it return a definite type instead (throw, `Option`, or empty).
sins.suggestion: Add a resolve-or-throw `get()` beside `find()`, or return `Option<T>`.

sins.name: deep-nesting
sins.description: `if` nested 3-deep (a pyramid — hoist guards / extract)
sins.rule: Flatten with guard clauses — never nest `if`s three deep into a pyramid.

sins.name: derived-argument
sins.description: Passing the same object twice — once whole and once broken into a piece (`persist($request, $request->shopId())`), or broken into several pieces at once (`new AgentTurn($r->output(), $r->failed(), $r->errorOutput())`) — when the callee could derive each piece itself from the one object.
sins.rule: Pass the object itself, not values derived from it — if a callee needs several pieces off one object, give it the object once and let it work out the rest.
sins.suggestion: Give the parameter the subject's type and move the derivations inside the callee; the call site then says what it means instead of spelling out the pieces.

sins.name: divergent-twin
sins.description: Two functions do the same job, but one of them skips a step the other takes — usually a fix made in one copy and forgotten in the other.
sins.rule: Put shared behaviour in one place, so a step that must always happen can't be forgotten in a copy.
sins.suggestion: Make the shorter function call the longer one, or have both call one shared function.

sins.name: duplicate-function
sins.description: Copy-pasted code — two+ functions with an identical AST (formatting/comments aside)
sins.rule: Extract copy-pasted code — two functions with an identical AST must become one.

sins.name: duplicated-mechanism
sins.description: Two or more classes in different files assemble the SAME rare set of collaborators — the same mechanism written twice in different words, so the decision behind it is made differently in each
sins.rule: Before writing a mechanism, search for the concept, not the exact name you had in mind. If it already exists twice, merge the two copies into one class every caller can use, instead of adding a third.
sins.suggestion: Extract the shared mechanism into one class the callers depend on, and delete the copies.

sins.name: enum-case-or-chain
sins.description: `$x === Enum::A || $x === Enum::B` — a hand-rolled case-group test
sins.rule: Put case-group membership on the enum (a method); don't hand-roll `$x === Enum::A || $x === Enum::B`.
sins.suggestion: A membership method on the enum (`$x->isFinal()`).

sins.name: enum-value-match
sins.description: A `match`/`switch` over an enum's `->value` at the call site — logic that belongs on the enum but lives elsewhere instead.
sins.rule: Put per-case behaviour on the enum; never `match`/`switch` over its `->value` at a call site.
sins.suggestion: A method on the backed enum (`$x->label()`, `$x->isPaid()`).

sins.name: erased-null-object
sins.description: A blank-rendering Null Object written into a `string` slot — coerced back to `''`
sins.rule: A Null Object only models absence while the TYPE admits it; never hand one to a `string`-typed slot, which coerces it to `''` and erases it.
sins.suggestion: Widen the type to carry the object (`Stringable`, or the class itself) where the Null Object is the point; otherwise drop the wrapper — and where the blank meant "missing", say that in the type with `?string` or an `Option<string>`.

sins.name: feature-envy
sins.description: Exiled behaviour / feature envy — a method operating on ONE other owned object's internals that belongs ON that object
sins.rule: Behaviour belongs with its data — move a method that loops or queries one other owned object onto that object.
sins.suggestion: Move the method onto the object (`$node->edges()`).

sins.name: flag-argument
sins.description: a method whose whole body branches on a `bool` parameter — or on whether a nullable one was given — two methods sharing one name
sins.rule: Split a method whose body is one branch on a flag into two NAMED methods — never make a call site say `true`, and never widen a required parameter to `?T = null` so that leaving it out means 'all of them'.
sins.suggestion: name each half for what it does (`renderCompact()` / `renderFull()`), with any shared middle as a private method both call

sins.name: generic-exception
sins.description: `throw new <bare SPL>` (RuntimeException/LogicException/…) instead of a named type
sins.rule: Throw a NAMED domain exception, never a bare SPL `Exception`/`RuntimeException`.
sins.suggestion: A named exception class with a static `::for($values)` factory that writes the message.

sins.name: hand-rolled-wither
sins.description: A wither method rebuilds the whole object by re-listing every constructor field, so adding a new field means updating every wither in the class.
sins.rule: A wither should only say what changes: `clone($this, ['x' => $x])` states the intent, while re-listing every field just repeats the constructor in every wither.
sins.suggestion: Replace `new self($this->a, $this->b, $changed)` with `clone($this, ['c' => $changed])` — `repent` does it for you.

sins.name: if-else-ladder
sins.description: if/elseif ladder of 4+ branches (should be match/dispatch)
sins.rule: Replace a 4+ branch if/elseif ladder with a `match`, a method on the type, or polymorphic dispatch.
sins.suggestion: A `match`, a method on the type, or polymorphic dispatch.

sins.name: in-array-mirrors-enum
sins.description: `in_array($x, [literals])` whose literals mirror an existing enum's cases
sins.rule: Test membership against the enum (its `cases()`/`tryFrom`), not an `in_array` of literals that mirror its values.
sins.suggestion: Use the enum (`Enum::tryFrom($x)` / a `cases()` check).

sins.name: inline-docblock
sins.description: A docblock whose delimiter shares a line with its text — a one-liner, or a block that opens or closes next to content
sins.rule: Write a docblock as a block: the opening delimiter on its own line, one star per line of content, the closing delimiter on its own line.
sins.suggestion: expand it — `repent` does this for you

sins.name: inline-throw
sins.description: `?? throw` fed into a call or dereferenced on the same line (inline throw mid-expression)
sins.rule: Guard at the top with an early `throw`; don't bury a `?? throw` mid-expression feeding further work.

sins.name: keyed-lookup-envy
sins.description: Indirect feature envy — a method that uses an owned object's IDENTITY as a key to look up a fact about it through a collaborator
sins.rule: Ask the object directly; don't use its identity as a key to look its own fact up through a collaborator.
sins.suggestion: Move the lookup onto the object that owns the identity.

sins.name: boundary-duplicated-operation
sins.description: The same domain operation hand-rolled at two DIFFERENT entry boundaries (a console command and an MCP tool, a controller and a command) — one operation with two implementations that drift
sins.rule: One operation, one implementation. A boundary translates its own protocol and calls the shared application service; it does not re-spell the operation.
sins.suggestion: Hoist the shared sequence into one application service and have both faces call it.

sins.name: config-read
sins.description: `config('…')` read inside a class
sins.rule: Inject a typed config object; never read `config('…')` inside a class.
sins.suggestion: Inject a typed config value object.

sins.name: container-reach
sins.description: `app()`/`resolve()` reach inside a container-resolved class
sins.rule: Declare dependencies in the constructor; never reach into the container with `app()`/`resolve()` from a resolved class.
sins.suggestion: Declare the dependency as a constructor parameter.

sins.name: dangling-route-name
sins.description: A `route('x')` lookup naming a route no registration mints — a stringly cross-reference that only fails at runtime, as a 500
sins.rule: The route-name vocabulary is a CLOSED set: every name looked up must be a name some route registers. Renaming a route means renaming its references in the same breath.
sins.suggestion: Point the lookup at the registered name, or register the route the name promises.

sins.name: dead-config-key
sins.description: A config key nothing reads — dead surface left behind by a deleted feature, which new code may wrongly adopt
sins.rule: Config is an interface: every key exists because something reads it. When the last reader goes, the key goes with it.
sins.suggestion: Delete the key (and its env var), or restore the reader the feature lost.

sins.name: dead-event-wiring
sins.description: An `Event::listen` on an event class no live code path can fire — a listener chain that dead-ends but reads as live wiring
sins.rule: A listener exists to answer a dispatch. When the last dispatcher goes, the listener goes with it.
sins.suggestion: Delete the registration (and the listener, if nothing else reaches it) — or restore the dispatch the listener was waiting for.

sins.name: duplicate-route
sins.description: Two route registrations of the same verb bind different URLs to the SAME `[Controller, method]` — two names for one handler (invokable single-action controllers, commonly aliased to several canonical URLs, are exempt)
sins.rule: Register a `[Controller, method]` action once; a second URL onto the same handler is a maintenance trap (names, middleware, constraints drift). An invokable controller mapped to several canonical URLs is fine.
sins.suggestion: Keep one route; if a second URL is truly needed, make it a redirect, or an invokable controller.

sins.name: duplicate-route-action
sins.description: Two route actions in different controllers thinly delegate to the SAME operation (`return $this->exporter->export(...)`) — the same entry point twice
sins.rule: One operation, one entry point — collapse duplicate thin actions to a single action (or two routes onto one), with the work in the shared service.
sins.suggestion: Delete the duplicate action and point its route at the surviving one (or a redirect).

sins.name: duplicated-config-default
sins.description: A config key whose default is stated TWICE — once in the config file, again as the reader's inline fallback — two sources of truth that drift silently
sins.rule: The config FILE owns the default. A reader asks for the value; it does not restate what the value should be when absent.
sins.suggestion: Drop the reader's fallback and let the config file answer — or delete the key from the file and let the reader's default be the one truth.

sins.name: facade-call
sins.description: Laravel facade call (`Cache::`, `Log::`, `Mail::` …)
sins.rule: Inject the dependency; never call a Laravel facade (`Cache::`, `Log::`, `Mail::`) inside a class.
sins.suggestion: Constructor-inject the dependency behind its interface.

sins.name: mass-update-at-call-site
sins.description: Bare `$model->update([...])` mass-array update at a call site
sins.rule: Mutate a model through an intention method; never `$model->update([...])` an anonymous array of columns at a call site.
sins.suggestion: An intention method on the model (`$order->markPaid()`).

sins.name: model-mutation-at-call-site
sins.description: Set-property-then-`save()` at a call site (should be an intention method)
sins.rule: Mutate a model through an intention method; don't set-property-then-`save()` at a call site.
sins.suggestion: An intention method on the model (`$order->suspend($reason)`).

sins.name: orphaned-binding
sins.description: A container binding whose abstract nothing ever resolves — dead wiring that reads as load-bearing and survives every refactor
sins.rule: Wiring is code: a binding exists to answer a resolve. When the last consumer goes, the binding goes with it.
sins.suggestion: Delete the registration (and the implementation it names, if that is dead too).

sins.name: raw-request-input
sins.description: Raw `->input()/->get()/->query()/->post()` on a Request
sins.rule: Read request input through a typed accessor (`$request->string('x')`); never raw `->input()`/`->get()`/`->query()`.
sins.suggestion: A named getter on a `FormRequest` subclass (`$request->productId()`).

sins.name: request-accessor-recast
sins.description: Re-coercing a typed request accessor at a call site — `$request->string('id')->toString()` or `(string) $request->string('id')` instead of a named getter on a request class
sins.rule: Expose a named getter on a typed request class; don't re-coerce a typed accessor (`$request->string('id')->toString()`) at a call site.
sins.suggestion: A named getter on a typed request class returning the coerced value.

sins.name: route-delegates-to-controller
sins.description: A route action forwards to ANOTHER controller's action (`return $this->otherController->action(...)`) — a redundant entry point onto an operation that already has one
sins.rule: A route action delegates INTO the domain (a service/action class), never sideways into another controller.
sins.suggestion: Extract the shared work into a service both routes call, or point the route at the real action and delete the wrapper.

sins.name: loop-inverted-guard
sins.description: Loop body (multi-statement) wrapped in an `if` instead of `continue` guard
sins.rule: Use a `continue` guard so the loop body stays flat; don't wrap the whole body in an `if`.

sins.name: manufactured-fake-fill
sins.description: `?? <empty literal>` filling a required slot (manufactured fake)
sins.rule: Fix an absent value at its source; never fill a required slot with a manufactured `?? ''`/`?? 0`/`?? []`.
sins.suggestion: Throw a named exception at the boundary, or bake a real default into the signature.

sins.name: masked-invariant
sins.description: Masked invariant — an own field read as `?->… ?? <fake literal>`, even though the very operation sets that field first, so the fallback only ever answers an impossible "not set yet".
sins.rule: Make an invariant certain (hold it non-nullable / assert it); don't mask it with `?->… ?? <fake>`.

sins.name: match-default-returns-null
sins.description: `match` `default` that returns `null`/`false`/`[]` (or has no body) instead of throwing
sins.rule: A `match`/`switch` `default` for an unhandled case must throw, not return `null`/`false`/`[]`.
sins.suggestion: `default => throw Unhandled::for($x)`.

sins.name: member-after-method
sins.description: A trait use, constant, property, property hook, or enum case declared below a method — so the reader only meets that state after seeing the behaviour that uses it.
sins.rule: Declare what a class HAS above what it DOES: trait uses, constants, properties and hooks stand at the top, above the constructor — never between two methods or appended at the bottom.

sins.name: member-out-of-order
sins.description: A declaration in the head of a class that arrives after something belonging below it — a constant under a property, a public field under a private one, a hook above the fields it reads
sins.rule: Order the head of a class the same way every time: trait uses, enum cases, constants, static properties, then instance properties public → protected → private, and hooked (derived) properties last, after the fields they read from.

sins.name: message-at-throw
sins.description: Message string built at the throw site (no domain values / named factory)
sins.rule: Pass domain VALUES to a named factory; never assemble the message string at the throw site.
sins.suggestion: A static `::for($values)` factory on the exception that builds the sentence.

sins.name: mutable-static-state
sins.description: A write to a static property — really a global variable with a namespace attached — where whichever write happens last wins, so the order code runs in changes the result.
sins.rule: Hold changing state on an INSTANCE someone owns and passes; never write a static property.
sins.suggestion: Constructor-inject the state as a collaborator, so who holds it (and who may change it) is written down.

sins.name: mutable-value-object
sins.description: A value type that mutates its own field after construction, so two things holding what should be the same value can end up different — one changes without the other knowing.
sins.rule: Make a value immutable: build it complete and derive a NEW one to change it; never write its fields after construction.
sins.suggestion: `readonly` on the class, and a `with…()`/named derivation that returns a new instance (PHP 8.5's `clone with`).

sins.name: namespace-cycle
sins.description: two namespaces that reference each other — neither can be read, tested or moved alone
sins.rule: Break every namespace cycle — dependencies point ONE way, so a namespace can always be lifted out on its own.
sins.suggestion: cut the weaker arrow: move the shared class down, or have the lower namespace own an interface the higher one implements

sins.name: namespace-dependency
sins.description: a declared layer references a layer it may not use (the arrow points back up)
sins.rule: Reference only DOWN the declared stack — a layer may use the layers it declared in `mayUse`, and nothing else that is declared.
sins.suggestion: invert the arrow: take the value/contract the low layer needs, and let the high layer supply it

sins.name: narrated-command
sins.description: A command named in the third person — `hides()`, `entersTestMode()` — where a call is an order, not a description of one
sins.rule: Name a command in the imperative: `hide()`, `enterTestMode()`, `openFor(\$user)` — never the third-person `hides()`, and never a participle.
sins.suggestion: drop the -s: the call site is giving the order, not narrating it

sins.name: near-duplicate-function
sins.description: Redundant methods — two+ functions with the same SHAPE differing only in names/literals (type-2 clone)
sins.rule: Collapse type-2 clones — two functions with the same shape (differing only in names/literals) become one parameterised function.

sins.name: negative-space-comment
sins.description: A comment defending the code against a strawman ("not random", "no magic", "not a coincidence", "not dead code")
sins.rule: State what the code IS, affirmatively — a comment that defends it against a strawman (that it is "not random", "no magic", "not a typo") is negative space; make the code self-evident and delete the comment.

sins.name: nested-ternary
sins.description: Nested/chained ternary `$a ? $b : ($c ? $d : $e)` (hidden control flow)
sins.rule: Unfold a nested/chained ternary into a `match` or guards; don't hide branching in `$a ? $b : ($c ? $d : $e)`.
sins.suggestion: A `match`, or early-return guards.

sins.name: non-counting-for
sins.description: A `for` loop that looks like it's counting, but its step actually assigns the next item instead of incrementing a counter.
sins.rule: Keep `for` for a counted loop, whose step advances a counter; walk with a `while`, or let the type hand out its own sequence.
sins.suggestion: A `while` over an explicit cursor — or better, an iterator on the type being walked, so the caller never holds the cursor at all.

sins.name: nullable-callback
sins.description: Nullable callback normalised in the body instead of a Null Object default
sins.rule: Default an optional callback to a Null Object in the signature; don't null-normalise a `?callable` in the body.
sins.suggestion: Create a reusable no-op invokable (`Invokable` + `NoOp`) and default the param to `new NoOp`.

sins.name: nullable-registry-lookup
sins.description: A keyed-store `get()` that returns `null` on a miss (should resolve-or-throw)
sins.rule: A keyed store's `get()` resolves-or-throws on a miss; don't return `null`.
sins.suggestion: `get()` returns-or-throws a named `…NotFound::forKey($key)`.

sins.name: param-resolved-from-param
sins.description: Unpacking the target out of a container parameter — a method takes `(Workflow $workflow, string $nodeId)` and resolves `$workflow->graph->nodeById($nodeId)` itself, when it could just receive the node directly.
sins.rule: Demand the resolved object you need; don't take a container + key and unpack the target yourself — the caller resolves once and passes it.
sins.suggestion: Take the resolved object as the param; resolve once in the caller.

sins.name: phantom-nullable
sins.description: Phantom nullable — a field typed `?T` (promoted param or declared property, any class) whose value, traced through the whole program, is always read as present and NEVER guarded, so the null never happens
sins.rule: If a nullable field is assumed present everywhere its value flows and guarded nowhere, the null is a lie — make it non-nullable and let it be required, failing hard at construction on a real miss.

sins.name: option-as-nullable
sins.description: `Option<T>` used as if it were nullable — `?Option`, `Option | null`, `unwrapOr(null)`
sins.rule: Use `Option` as a real option (`some`/`none`/`match`); never `?Option`/`Option | null`/`unwrapOr(null)`.
sins.suggestion: Wrap at the seam with `Option::fromNullable($x)`, then consume with `match`/`unwrapOr`.

sins.name: positional-tuple-return
sins.description: Returning a positional TUPLE — `return [$node, $key, $inputs, $outputs]` — bundling independent values as a keyless list the caller destructures by position
sins.rule: Return a typed object, not a positional tuple `[$a, $b, $c]` the caller destructures by position.
sins.suggestion: A small `readonly` result object.

sins.name: raw-decoded-array-return
sins.description: Returning a raw decoded boundary array (`json_decode(...)`) untyped
sins.rule: Return a typed object from a decoded boundary; never hand back a raw `json_decode(...)` array.
sins.suggestion: Decode into a Spatie `Data` object: `X::from(json_decode(...))`.

sins.name: redundant-arrow-return-type
sins.description: An arrow function whose return type only repeats what its one expression provably yields — `fn (): string => $this->name` on a `string` property
sins.rule: Leave the return type off an arrow function whose expression already proves the type. Declare one when the type is genuinely ambiguous or you are narrowing it — never to restate a property or a method you can read from here.
sins.suggestion: drop the `: Type` — `repent` does this for you

sins.name: redundant-else
sins.description: `else` after an `if` branch that already returns/throws (redundant)
sins.rule: Drop the `else` after an `if` branch that already returns/throws/continues/breaks.

sins.name: repeated-guard
sins.description: The SAME compound guard condition recurs in ≥2 places — the same check spelled differently (inline reaches vs locals) or reordered still counts, so a copied condition has no name
sins.rule: Promote a recurring compound guard to a named predicate. The same condition — however its conjuncts are ordered, and whether it reads `$obj->x` inline or a local aliased from it — belongs in ONE named method.
sins.suggestion: Extract the repeated condition into a named boolean method and call THAT at each site.

sins.name: repeated-named-call
sins.description: The same `with`-style (variadic) method is called with the same named argument at 2+ sites, instead of a named helper on the type
sins.rule: Promote a repeated `->with…(named: …)` call into a method on the receiver's type that hides the call and its construction boilerplate.
sins.suggestion: `$element->withMetadata($payload)` — a `withMetadata()` on the type doing `copyWith(metadata: $payload->toArray())`.

sins.name: repeated-type-guard
sins.description: The SAME multi-`instanceof` type-narrowing guard (`$x instanceof A && $x->y instanceof B`) is written verbatim in ≥2 places — a check with no name, copied instead of named
sins.rule: Promote a recurring `instanceof` chain to a named predicate (`$x->isNewOfNamedClass()`), so the intent has a name and the narrowing has ONE home.
sins.suggestion: Extract the repeated `instanceof` chain into a named boolean method and call THAT at each site.

sins.name: restated-comment
sins.description: An inline comment that only spells the statement below it back in prose ("// save the order" over `$this->orders->save($order)`)
sins.rule: An inline comment must say something the code does not — never narrate the statement below it; if every word of the comment is already a word of the code, delete the comment.

sins.name: scratch-state-restore
sins.description: Scratch state on `$this` — a method that saves one of its own fields to a local and restores it (`$prev = $this->scope; … $this->scope = $prev`), the field really a per-call input
sins.rule: Pass a per-call value as a parameter; don't save-and-restore one of your own fields as scratch state.

sins.name: short-circuit-statement
sins.description: a bare `$a && $b->do();` statement — a short-circuit whose result nothing reads, so the operator is an `if` in disguise
sins.rule: Branch with an `if`; never run work off the right side of a bare `&&`/`||` statement whose result nothing reads.

sins.name: all-nullable-data
sins.description: All-nullable "god" DTO — every field `?T`/defaulted (type doesn't tell the truth)
sins.rule: A DTO's field types must tell the truth — make required fields non-nullable; don't default every field to `?T`/null. If every field genuinely IS optional and same-shaped (a callback bag, a filter set, a money breakdown), make each non-nullable with a Null Object / identity default on the value type instead. "But the fields ARE genuinely optional" is the trigger for this fix, NOT an exemption from it: genuine absence is exactly what `T|Optional = new Optional()` models — for ANY `Data` (it is unrelated to `#[TypeScript]`) — so "no identity value fits" / "a wire null is honest" means reach for `Optional`, never leave every field `?T = null`.
sins.suggestion: Retype each field to the truth: required → non-nullable, no default; genuinely-absent → `T|Optional = new Optional()` (dropped from output, not `null`); always-present-but-emptyable → a Null Object / identity default (`Grid $grid = new Grid()`, `Status $s = Status::Default`). If a whole SUB-object may be absent, put the optional on the CONTAINER field (`Type|Optional $x = new Optional()`) and keep that type's leaves concrete — don't scatter `?T`/`Optional` across every leaf.

sins.name: all-optional-data
sins.description: Every field of a `Data` object is `T|Optional` — the type promises nothing is ever present; the absence belongs on the CONTAINER field where it's used
sins.rule: Don't make every field of a Data object `Optional` (the all-nullable smell in another skin). Almost always it's the WHOLE object that is present-or-absent — mark the enclosing field `Type|Optional` at its use site and give this object honest, concrete leaves, so if it exists it's a valid whole.
sins.suggestion: Give each leaf a concrete default (`int $columns = 1`) and move the optionality up to where this type is used: `public readonly Grid|Optional $grid = new Optional();`.

sins.name: constructor-orchestration
sins.description: A page object fills a public slot imperatively in the constructor (`$this->x = $this->projector->…()`) where a `#[Computed]` property hook would describe it in place
sins.rule: Project each self-contained page-object slot in a `#[Computed]` get-hook, not an imperative constructor assignment.
sins.suggestion: Replace `$this->x = expr;` with `#[Computed] public T $x { get => expr; }`. Pin a deliberately-eager slot (one that must capture request-scoped state at build time) with `#[Eager]` — the scaffolded escape hatch.

sins.name: data-collection-type
sins.description: A `Data` property is TYPED as `DataCollection` — it should be `array` (or `Collection`) with `#[DataCollectionOf(X)]`; the `DataCollection` type emits malformed TypeScript and skips element-typed hydration
sins.rule: Never type a `Data` property as `DataCollection`. Type it `array` (preferred) or `Collection` and add `#[DataCollectionOf(X::class)]` — element typing drives hydration, nested validation, and clean TypeScript.
sins.suggestion: `#[DataCollectionOf(NodeData::class)] public readonly array $nodes;`, not `public readonly DataCollection $nodes;`.

sins.name: data-method-hint-collision
sins.description: `@method` tag that re-declares a real method (names the concrete factory, not the magic `from`/`collect`)
sins.rule: A `@method` hint must name the magic `from`/`collect`, never re-declare a real method (no IDE collision).

sins.name: data-to-array-roundtrip
sins.description: A `X::from(...)->toArray()` sits in a `::from` slot typed `X` that re-hydrates it — build → array → build
sins.rule: Don't `->toArray()` a `Data` into a slot that re-hydrates it; pass the object (or the source array) directly.
sins.suggestion: Drop the `->toArray()` — the nested-`Data` / `#[DataCollectionOf]` slot takes the object as-is.

sins.name: derived-collection-cast
sins.description: A `#[DataCollectionOf]` is filled by mapping a factory over inputs at the call site, where a `#[WithCast]` should own the derivation
sins.rule: Move an element derivation (`array_map(E::for(...), $xs)`) into a `#[WithCast]` / `IterableItemCast` on the collection property; pass the raw list.
sins.suggestion: `#[WithCast(SomeCast::class)] public array $items` — the cast runs `E::for(...)` per item; the call site passes the raw values.

sins.name: flat-field-cluster
sins.description: A `#[TypeScript]` `Data` class spreads a value object it already models flat across sibling scalar fields sharing a camelCase prefix (`wireType` + `wireLabel`) instead of nesting the existing `Wire{type, label}`.
sins.rule: When scalar fields on a Data class share a prefix that names a value object the codebase already declares, they restate that object flat. Nest them into the existing sub-object and shed the prefix — `wireType`/`wireLabel` become `wire: Wire{type, label}`.
sins.suggestion: Replace the prefixed siblings with a single nested property typed as the existing value object, dropping the prefix from each member.

sins.name: hand-key-remap
sins.description: A `::from([...])` mechanically renames `$src['snake_key']` → `camelKey` by hand, instead of a class-level `#[MapInputName]`
sins.rule: Map a snake_case boundary with one class-level `#[MapInputName(SnakeCaseMapper::class)]` + `::from($src)`, not a hand-written key translation.
sins.suggestion: `#[MapInputName(SnakeCaseMapper::class)]` on the class, then `SomeData::from($src)`.

sins.name: hook-missing-computed
sins.description: A get-only property HOOK on a `Data` class lacks `#[Computed]` — Spatie reads the virtual property as a hydration INPUT, expects it in `::from()`, and crashes or silently drops it
sins.rule: Mark every get-only property hook on a `Data` class `#[Computed]`, so Spatie treats it as an output-only computed value, not a required hydration input.
sins.suggestion: Add `#[Computed]` above the property: `#[Computed] public array $docks { get => $this->dockSet->all(); }`.

sins.name: injected-service-not-hidden
sins.description: A page object injects a service (`#[FromContainer]`, …) into a public property without `#[Hidden]` — it leaks into the generated TypeScript type
sins.rule: Every injected collaborator on a page object carries `#[Hidden]`, so the service never serializes or reaches the frontend type.
sins.suggestion: Add `#[Hidden]` above the injection attribute to keep it off the wire. To also keep it out of the generated TypeScript, wire the scaffolded hidden-aware transformer into your typescript-transformer config — otherwise LaravelData's `#[Hidden]` alone still leaks the property into the TS type.

sins.name: manual-hydration-loop
sins.description: Collections hydrated with `::from()` per item instead of `#[DataCollectionOf]` + `::collect()`
sins.rule: Hydrate a collection with `#[DataCollectionOf]` + `::collect()`, not a per-item `::from()` loop.
sins.suggestion: `#[DataCollectionOf(X::class)]` + `X::collect($rows)`.

sins.name: manual-input-cast
sins.description: A `Data` value-object property is hand-built at every construction site, instead of a `#[WithCast]` / `Castable` that owns the hydration once
sins.rule: Hydrate a value-object property with a `#[WithCast]` (or a `Castable` value object), never by hand-building it at every `new`/`::from` call site.
sins.suggestion: Type the property as the value object and add `#[WithCast(SomeCast::class)]` (or make the value object `Castable`) so the `simple → complex` mapping lives in one place.

sins.name: manual-output-transform
sins.description: A `Data` computed slot hand-flattens a value object into a wire array, instead of a `#[WithTransformer]` that owns the serialized shape
sins.rule: Shape a property's wire output with a `#[WithTransformer]` (+ a matching `#[TypeScriptType]`), never a computed getter that hand-builds the reshaped array.
sins.suggestion: Keep the real value-object type and add `#[WithTransformer(SomeTransformer::class)]` — plus `#[TypeScriptType(...)]` so the generated TypeScript matches the transformed shape.

sins.name: nested-type-missing-typescript
sins.description: A `#[TypeScript]` Data has a property typed as a nested `Data` class that itself lacks `#[TypeScript]` — the transformer emits it as `undefined`, a silent hole in the generated type (a nested enum is fine; the enum collector auto-generates it)
sins.rule: Every nested `Data` reachable on the wire from a `#[TypeScript]` class must ALSO be `#[TypeScript]` (or the property must declare its shape with `#[LiteralTypeScriptType]`), or it generates as `undefined`. Enums need no tag — they auto-generate.
sins.suggestion: Add `#[TypeScript]` to the nested `Data` class the property points at.

sins.name: new-data-object
sins.description: `new <Data subclass>` instead of `::from()` / a `fromX()` factory
sins.rule: Build a rich `Data` object via `::from()`/a `fromX()` factory, never `new`.
sins.suggestion: `X::from(...)` (or a `fromY()` factory).

sins.name: non-final-data
sins.description: Data class not `final` / props not `readonly` promoted
sins.rule: Seal a Data class `final` with `readonly` promoted props — it's a leaf, not a base.

sins.name: null-to-optional-map
sins.description: A producer hand-maps null→`new Optional` — `$x === null ? new Optional : Foo::from($x)` or `expr() ?? new Optional` — instead of one named factory (Spatie's `optional()` maps null→null, the opposite of what a `T|Optional` slot needs)
sins.rule: Map an absent value onto `Optional` in ONE named factory, not a ternary at every producer. Use the scaffolded `optionalOrMissing()` (null → `new Optional`, else `::from`), the omit-from-wire counterpart to Spatie's `optional()`.
sins.suggestion: Replace `$x === null ? new Optional : Foo::from($x)` / `expr() ?? new Optional` with `Foo::optionalOrMissing($x)` (scaffold the `OptionalOrMissing` trait).

sins.name: nullable-wire-object
sins.description: A nested object on a `#[TypeScript]` Data is typed `T | null` — it ships `null` on the wire where `T | Optional` would OMIT it (what the frontend's `x?.` reads for "absent")
sins.rule: On a `#[TypeScript]` (frontend-bound) Data, type a genuinely-absent nested object `T | Optional = new Optional()`, not `T | null` — so the wire omits it rather than carrying a `null`.
sins.suggestion: `public readonly UiChrome|Optional $chrome = new Optional();`, not `public readonly UiChrome|null $chrome = null;`.

sins.name: page-object-missing-typescript
sins.description: A page object travels back in a response but carries no `#[TypeScript]` — the `.vue` page reads it as untyped `any`, so the whole page-prop contract goes unchecked
sins.rule: Annotate every page object `#[TypeScript]` so it generates a frontend type the page binds against — a response-bound Data with no annotation is a type-safety hole.
sins.suggestion: Add `#[TypeScript]` above the page-object class (`use Spatie\TypeScriptTransformer\Attributes\TypeScript;`).

sins.name: placeholder-filled-data
sins.description: A required non-nullable `string` slot handed `''` — the type promises a value that is always there and the caller has none
sins.rule: A required slot means the caller has the value. Filling it just to satisfy the type signature hides a missing value in a way no type check can catch.
sins.suggestion: Fetch the real value, or split off a narrower type that only promises the fields you actually have.

sins.name: prefer-optional-create
sins.description: A raw `new Optional` is constructed in a runtime expression where Spatie's built-in `Optional::create()` factory reads clearer
sins.rule: Use `Optional::create()`, not `new Optional`, everywhere a static call is legal — a parameter/property default must stay `new Optional` (a factory call is illegal there), everywhere else prefer the factory.
sins.suggestion: Replace `new Optional` / `new Optional()` with `Optional::create()`.

sins.name: redundant-enum-unwrap
sins.description: An enum is unwrapped to `->value` at a hydration site (`'status' => $order->status->value`) where the property is typed as that enum — Spatie re-casts the scalar straight back to the enum
sins.rule: Pass the enum itself to an enum slot — Spatie's enum cast keeps it; don't destructure it to `->value` at the hydration site only for it to be re-hydrated.
sins.suggestion: `'status' => $order->status`, not `'status' => $order->status->value`.

sins.name: redundant-native-cast
sins.description: An enum / date is constructed at a hydration site (`Enum::from($x)`, `new DateTime($x)`) where the property auto-casts the raw scalar
sins.rule: Pass the raw scalar to an enum / `DateTimeInterface` slot — Spatie auto-casts it; don't construct the value at the hydration site.
sins.suggestion: `'status' => $raw`, not `'status' => Status::from($raw)`.

sins.name: redundant-nested-from
sins.description: A nested `X::from([...])` fills a slot the parent `::from` already auto-hydrates from the array
sins.rule: Pass the plain array for a nested `Data` / `#[DataCollectionOf]` slot — don't wrap it in `X::from([...])`.
sins.suggestion: `'slot' => ['a' => 1]` (or `[['a' => 1], ...]` for a collection), not `X::from(['a' => 1])`.

sins.name: service-location-in-page-object
sins.description: A page object reaches into the container with `app()`/`resolve()` instead of injecting the collaborator via `#[FromContainer]`
sins.rule: A page object pulls every collaborator through `#[FromContainer]` (hidden), never `app()`/`resolve()` inside a getter.
sins.suggestion: Inject it as a `#[Hidden] #[FromContainer(Service::class)]` constructor property.

sins.name: transformer-without-ts-type
sins.description: A `#[WithTransformer]` changes a property's wire shape but has no paired `#[TypeScriptType]`/`#[LiteralTypeScriptType]`, so the generated TypeScript keeps the wrong (PHP) type
sins.rule: Pair every custom `#[WithTransformer]` with a `#[TypeScriptType]` / `#[LiteralTypeScriptType]` that declares the transformed wire shape.
sins.suggestion: Add `#[TypeScriptType('...')]` (or `#[LiteralTypeScriptType(...)]`) stating the type the transformer serializes to, so the generated frontend type matches the wire.

sins.name: stacked-docblock
sins.description: Two or more docblocks stacked on one declaration — PHP reads only the last, so the ones above it are documentation nobody sees
sins.rule: One declaration carries ONE docblock — merge a stack into a single block, because the language hands only the last one to a reader's tooling.
sins.suggestion: merge them into one block — `repent` does this for you

sins.name: string-match-mirrors-enum
sins.description: `match`/`switch` over string/int literals that mirror an existing backed enum's case values
sins.rule: Dispatch over the enum's cases, not string/int literals that mirror its values.
sins.suggestion: Dispatch via a method on the backed enum's cases.

sins.name: swallow-catch
sins.description: `catch` whose only effect is `return null/false/[]`; empty catch (silent swallow)
sins.rule: Let a failure throw, or surface it named with the cause; never swallow a catch into `null`/`false`/`[]`/`none()` or an empty body.
sins.suggestion: Rethrow wrapped (`previous: $e`), or catch-log-skip at one named boundary.

sins.name: ternary-statement
sins.description: a bare `$cond ? doThis() : doThat();` statement — a ternary whose value nothing reads, so it is choosing an ACTION, not a value
sins.rule: Choose an action with `if`/`else`; a ternary chooses a VALUE, so never write one whose result nothing reads.

sins.name: type-switch
sins.description: two or more `instanceof` tests on the same subject deciding different branches — asking a value what it IS instead of telling it what to do
sins.rule: Let each type answer for itself; never branch on what a value IS when a method on it could say what it DOES.
sins.suggestion: A method on the shared interface, implemented per type — so a new type needs no edit here at all.

sins.name: unnamed-vocabulary-literal
sins.description: A raw string in an argument the codebase elsewhere fills from a named vocabulary — `expect('{')` beside `expect(Token::COLON)`, where `Token::BRACE_OPEN` already names it
sins.rule: Where a parameter is spelled from a named vocabulary, spell it that way EVERYWHERE — never the raw value at one call site and the constant at the next.
sins.suggestion: The constant that already holds this value, referenced by name.

sins.name: useless-property-hook
sins.description: A `get` hook that reads nothing from `$this` — a stored property wearing computed syntax
sins.rule: A property hook must EARN its hook: a `get` body that references no `$this` (and no `parent::`) computes nothing from the object — it yields the same value however the instance is configured, so it is a plain property in disguise. This usually happens when an interface declares `{ get; }` and the implementer mimics the syntax; a plain property satisfies a hooked interface property just as well.
sins.suggestion: Make it a stored property: a constant body becomes a property default (`public ?Transition $t = null;`); a constructed value (`get => Transition::make(...)`) is assigned ONCE in the constructor. Keep the hook only when the body genuinely derives from `$this` state.

sins.name: wrapping-without-cause
sins.description: Wrapping a caught exception without passing it as `previous`/cause
sins.rule: When wrapping a caught exception, pass the original as `previous`/cause — never drop the stack trace.
sins.suggestion: Pass the caught exception as `previous: $e`.
